title: Cross-zone fleet stewardship: placement and soft-failover policies for regional dedicated pools
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a flexible placement and failover policy surface for regional dedicated fleets that supports: strict data residency, soft (graceful) failover between zones, throughput-guarantee knobs, and autoscaling headroom controls. This ticket covers the API, controller behavior, and an initial rollout plan for a single-customer pilot. The goal is to allow customers to express placement intent (preferred zones, hard-residency, spread vs packed) and to provide deterministic soft-failover that preserves throughput guarantees and avoids mass cold-starts during zone events.
background: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput and clear controls over where inference happens. Existing fleet placement is region-centric and fails over aggressively, which can trigger large-scale instance churn and spikes in latency/cost. We need a policy model that encodes residency, latency targets, throughput reservation, and controlled drift during failure: i.e., try to keep traffic in zone when possible, gracefully absorb load across remaining zones with reserved warm capacity, and fall back to hosted variants only when policy allows.
proposal: 1) Placement policy DSL: a small JSON/YAML schema that supports keys: residency (hard|soft|none), zone_preferences (ordered list), spread_policy (balanced|packed|prefer-local), throughput_guarantee (tokens_per_sec or rps), and burst_reserve (percent). 2) Autoscaling controls: configurable headroom, warm-pool size, scale-up cooldown and scale-down delay per policy so throughput guarantees are met without oscillation. 3) Soft-failover orchestration: when a zone degrades, controller drains new allocations from the degraded zone, routes existing active sessions according to KV-cache affinity rules, and brings warm instances up in target zones using reserved burst capacity before shifting traffic. 4) Audit and residency enforcement: every routing decision must include a residency decision log entry and KMS-tagged audit context for compliance customers. 5) Admin API + Console: operators can inspect policy evaluation, force-failover, or perform simulated failover to validate policies.
acceptance_criteria: Placement DSL implemented and documented in repository (schema + examples)
Controller respects 'hard' residency: no inference served outside region when set and returns 403/error when impossible
Soft-failover path demonstrates <2x latency P95 increase under simulated single-zone outage for pilot customer with throughput_guarantee=1000tps
Autoscaler supports headroom and warm-pool settings and respects cooldown windows to prevent flapping
Audit logs contain per-request residency decision and route path for customers with compliance enabled
E2E smoke test: simulated zone failure does not drop active sessions (connection-level simulation) for 95% of sessions in pilot run
Console shows policy evaluation timeline and a simulated-failover button for operator testing
implementation_notes: Add policy parser to FleetController and persist policy object on Fleet CR for Private and Dedicated control planes
Introduce warm-pool allocator with a small reservation queue per zone; allocator should support prioritized warm-starts for throughput_guarantee workloads
Enhance routing layer to include residency metadata in token lineage and to consult policy for reject/route decisions
Instrument KV-cache affinity: when moving active sessions, attempt cache-prefetch or replay where supported to avoid decoding cold caches
Security: residency enforcement requires KMS context marker for audit; coordinate with Security for HSM tagging flow
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and validation (invalid combos rejected)
Integration tests: policy applied to a multi-zone local cluster simulator, asserting placement and audit logs
Chaos test: inject zone latency and outage; assert autoscaler warm-pool behavior and soft-failover path metrics
Load test: validate throughput_guarantee under normal and degraded conditions with ~1k-10k concurrent requests
Compliance test: simulate 'hard' residency and verify request rejection when external capacity needed
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Internal alpha (week 1-2): implement DSL, controller hooks, and console UI behind feature flag; run unit/integration tests
Stage 2 - Canary pilot (week 3-4): enable for single pilot customer on Dedicated in us-west and us-east with SLA-backed throughput_guarantee; perform simulated-failover drills
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp (week 5-7): open to a small set of customers, monitor SLOs and cost delta, tighten autoscaler defaults
Stage 4 - GA (week 8): documentation and public API; migration guide for customers with existing placement expectations
monitoring_and_slo: SLO: 99.9% availability for region-local traffic when residency=soft and no more than 2x P95 latency increase during single-zone disruptions
Metrics to emit: policy_eval_latency_ms, warm_pool_fill_ratio, reserved_capacity_utilization, failover_transition_time_ms, residency_decisions_total{hard,soft,none}
Alerts: failover_transition_time_ms > 30s for 5m, warm_pool_fill_ratio < 0.2 for >10m during increased load
